Query Redshift as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__redshift.R
oauth_db_redshift.Rd

Read Redshift data in a Shiny app using each visitor's database permissions. The helper opens a DBI connection through Redshift's IAM Identity Center integration for SQL or dbplyr queries.

Usage

oauth_db_redshift(
  authorization,
  server,
  database,
  ...,
  driver = "Amazon Redshift (x64)",
  port = 5439L,
  token_type = c("EXT_JWT", "ACCESS_TOKEN"),
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

server

Database hostname.

database

Database name.

...

Named Redshift ODBC options, such as CaFile or LoginTimeout. The helper sets authentication and verified TLS.

driver

Installed ODBC driver name.

port

Database port.

token_type

"EXT_JWT" for an external provider's JWT access token, or "ACCESS_TOKEN" for an IAM Identity Center access token.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then pass the connection to DBI. Before sign-in, the function waits quietly.

Details

Install odbc and the Redshift ODBC 2.x driver with IdpTokenAuthPlugin. Configure IAM Identity Center to trust your sign-in provider and map users to database permissions. Your shinyOAuth client must obtain a token for the audience accepted by that integration.

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each query.

Connection lifetime

Connections open on first use and close after sign-out, account changes or session end. An established SQL connection stays open through ordinary token renewal; a new connection gets a current token.

See also

oauth_db_microsoft_client(). vignette("redshift", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_redshift(
  auth$connection,
  server = "cluster.example.eu-west-1.redshift.amazonaws.com",
  database = "reporting",
  token_type = "EXT_JWT"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user")
})
} # }
